title: hermes-runs-as-a-device-beside-cc
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(a_suspicion_becomes_a_sieve) -> PROVED
intention: hermes-agent runs as a Cairn DEVICE (instance 0) on this box beside CC — its inference out through the proxy and its own JSONL ledgers tailed into the device's diagnostic trail — so a second agent's thoughts AND its actions are both inspectable without forking it.
why: Law 8 (peers require trust, so prove first — it enters proven-space by grafting, one ticket at a time, and 3,977 upstream tests buy it nothing here); Law 10 (nothing in the system is immeasurable — a second agent is inside that set, not above it); Law 7 (its trail is a record of truth and may never collapse an error); Law 4 (the rule that it cannot red anything must be PHYSICS, not hermes' good manners).
how: A device directory with a charter and instance 0. Its model calls point at the OpenAI-shaped door (sibling intent) so cognition lands in the meter and the trail. Its own ledgers — skill_ledger.jsonl, the curator ledger — are tailed into the device's diagnostic trail through the existing diagnostic.py floor, so ACTION is recorded beside COGNITION. Its declared role is peer and antagonist: it files questions and troubles, and passes no gate, ever.
falsifier: DONE when hermes runs on this box; every model call it makes appears in inference_calls; every skill or memory mutation it makes appears in the device's trail; and it has filed at least one trouble or question that CC did not raise. WRONG INTENT if keeping it inspectable turns out to require forking it after all (the fork was the option this design exists to avoid), or if the antagonist produces suspicions nobody ever converts into a sieve — a peer whose findings never become physics is a second opinion, not a second party. MEASURED CONSTRAINT that may relocate rather than kill it: this box has 15GB total and ~9GB available, and CC has OOM-killed it three times at 12-14GB; if two agents cannot coexist here the device moves to Hex and the intent survives at a different address.
traces_to: Law 8 (peers require trust, so prove first — it enters proven-space by grafting, one ticket at a time, and 3,977 upstream tests buy it nothing here); Law 10 (nothing in the system is immeasurable — a second agent is inside that set, not above it); Law 7 (its trail is a record of truth and may never collapse an error); Law 4 (the rule that it cannot red anything must be PHYSICS, not hermes' good manners).

watchme.trigger: each trouble or question filed by the hermes device
watchme.enough: when 20 hermes-filed suspicions have been dispositioned — at that point the conversion rate to a deterministic sieve that actually fired is a measured number and the antagonist either pays for its RAM or does not
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier clause: at least one filed trouble or question CC did not raise, and the fraction of filed suspicions that became sieves
watchme.nexus: the trouble store plus the question corpus — the two places a suspicion can land, so the probe reads what exists rather than a new table
watchme.consumer: Akien, because whether a second agent earns its keep is a spec question his head settles, not a measurement-settled one

gates_bound: proof gate — proofs beside the code, run by the tester under netns isolation; teeth a hollow build could not pass (Law 8).
feeds back to origin on failure — a red routes to this ticket's own voyage, never to a paragraph (Law 3 + the deterministic-red rule: fixed, or carrying a ruling from Akien).
durability gate — not done until proven AND committed.

emit chokepoint — every crossing rides cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit at the component's own address carrying this ticket id; BUILDME refused without a berthed validate packet claiming it, PROVED refused without a complete passing verdict artifact.
owner: CC builds it; the hermes device owns its own instance state once it stands. Akien owns the design ratification — whether a second agent runs here at all is a spec question, not a measurement-settled one
owning_intention: cairn/devices/hermes/intention+why.json — TO BE WRITTEN BY THIS TICKET; the device does not exist yet
depends_on: QUEUED ON the OpenAI-door ticket (548dd13fb4db) (sibling, same idea). hermes' inference has nowhere metered to go until that door stands, and running it un-metered even once would make its first calls the only ones this system cannot see.

cast_checks.assumption_check: The unstated load-bearing assumption is a VALUE one, not a technical one: that a second agent's suspicions are worth ~6GB of a 15GB box. Nothing measures that, and the honest consequence is that the device must be instrumented for its conversion rate (suspicion to a sieve that fires) from the first day rather than after it has earned goodwill. A second assumption: that hermes' ledgers are tailable as an append-only stream — measured that skill_ledger writes JSONL with content-addressed manifests, NOT measured that it flushes in a way a tail can follow.
cast_checks.missing_check: Yes. 'Files questions and troubles' was asserted wrapped and is not: BOTH of those are doors with contracts, and whether a non-CC hand may fire them is an open Law 6 question. The trouble door and the question corpus each have an owner, and hermes is not in any gated_by list anywhere. This is the ticket's real edge and it is written here rather than discovered at BUILDME: hermes' output may have to land as a PROPOSAL that CC or Akien admits, not as a direct write.
cast_checks.falsifier_check: The intent's falsifier stands with one clause carrying the weight: it has filed at least one trouble or question CC did not raise. That is what distinguishes a running process from a peer, and it is why 'it starts' is explicitly not enough — aider_shim can already claim that and has 0 surviving edits. HORIZON: one week of running alongside CC. Wrong-intent tells are both written: needing to fork after all, and suspicions nobody converts. MEASURED RELOCATION CLAUSE rather than a kill: 15GB total, ~9GB available, CC has OOM-killed this box three times at 12-14GB; if they cannot coexist the device moves to Hex.
cast_checks.collision_check: Checked 'reaching for daemons is drift' — a DISTINCTION, and the whys separate cleanly. CLAUDE.md defines a device as a top-level thing that is ITS OWN PROCESS, so a long-lived hermes process is the rung's normal shape; the drift would be CAIRN growing a poller to watch it, and that is a bound for the charter. Checked Law 8 (peers require proof first): not a collision but a CONSTRAINT this ticket inherits — 3,977 upstream tests buy nothing here, and it grafts one ticket at a time. Checked 'nothing in inspectors or gates is allowed to be llm': not a collision because the role explicitly passes no gate, and that must be physics rather than manners.
cast_checks.builder_check: (1) WHERE: cairn/devices/hermes/0/ — device rung, instance 0, never a singleton exemption. (2) WHAT IT MAY NOT DO, and this needs to be physics not prose: it may not write a gate passage, may not seal a validation, may not appear in any charter's gated_by. A builder should ask how that is ENFORCED rather than declared; the honest first answer is that it holds no credential the doors accept, which is enforcement by Law 6 rather than by a check. (3) ITS INFERENCE: points at the OpenAI door (sibling ticket), which means THIS TICKET DEPENDS ON THAT ONE and should read queued on it rather than racing it. (4) ITS LEDGERS: tail skill_ledger.jsonl and the curator ledger into the device trail via cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py — compose the floor, do not author a receiver. (5) WHAT NOT TO BUILD: no poller, no scheduler on the Cairn side, no supervisor. (6) INSTALL: hermes ships a curl-pipe-bash installer from its own domain; run it in the constrained box and keep it away from ~/.cairn and both git roots on first run.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: (a) Fork and instrument inside — rejected on measurement: 922MB of .git, upstream at PR #107,000, so every pull becomes a merge, in order to obtain logging that inference_domain has produced since 2026-08-18 (one emission line per call carrying host, path, model, provider and the route walked). (b) Run it with no integration and read its files by hand — rejected because that is exactly the unmeasured state Akien named this morning as the 'working on myself' problem; an antagonist nobody can audit is a second voice, not a second measurement.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: aider_shim is the standing prior art and it is a WARNING, not an endorsement: a third-party coding agent already wrapped as a Cairn device, with the standing thread recording 0 surviving edits from it. That is evidence about how hard the shim pattern is, and it is why this intent's falsifier demands a FILED TROUBLE rather than a running process — 'it starts' is what aider_shim can already claim.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That a second agent's suspicions are worth 6GB of a 15GB box. Unmeasured. The number that would settle it is the conversion rate from hermes suspicion to a deterministic sieve that actually fires, and nothing measures that yet — which makes it the first thing the device should be instrumented for, not the last.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: With the standing rule 'reaching for daemons is drift': hermes runs a gateway process, watchdogs and a periodic scheduler. NOT terminal, and the whys differ. A DEVICE is by CLAUDE.md's own definition a top-level thing that is its own process, so a long-lived hermes process is the rung's normal shape. The drift would be CAIRN growing a poller to watch it — and that is a bound to write into the charter, not a reason to refuse.

children: none yet, but ONE IS LIKELY: if hermes may not fire the trouble and question doors directly (the open Law 6 edge in missing_check), an admission path becomes a child ticket. It is not cast now because the edge is a question, not a settled design.
